summary: This abstract class provides a helper method that converts an array of data into a collection of objects. The populate method loops through an array, instantiates a new object of a specified class for each item, copies the array data into that object's properties, and stores it in an internal collection.

explanations.2: The class implements Iterator, which is a PHP interface that lets you loop over this collection using foreach, but the class is abstract so you can't instantiate it directly—subclasses must implement the required Iterator methods.
explanations.6: new $dataobject() creates a new instance of a class whose name is stored in the $dataobject variable—this is called dynamic instantiation and lets you create different object types by passing different class names.
explanations.7: $object->$key = $val uses a variable variable name: $key contains the property name as a string, so $object->$key sets a property dynamically based on the array key.
explanations.8: $this->storage[] means we're appending the new object to an array called storage that belongs to this class instance.
